newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli budget chief warns against raising taxes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli budget chief warns against raising taxes.

text.p: The budget director at Israel's Treasury warned a parliamentary committee on Tuesday that proposals to cut subsidies to employers would undermine the economy's international competitiveness.

Ron Croll said proposals to reduce aid by some two billion shekels as a way of cutting the 1997 budget would be tantamount to a tax on employment. Such a measure would raise labour costs, slowing the economy and increasing unemployment, he said.
The government has been subsidising employers' social security payments.

Croll said parliament needed to approve the full budget cuts sought by the Treasury for 1997 without substituting new taxes in place of spending. In an interview with Israel Radio, Krol warned that the 4.9 billion shekel reduction the Treasury has proposed may not be enough and that further cuts would be sought later.

Parliament is now debating the Treasury's 190.8 billion shekel budget for 1997 and has until December 31 to approve it. The spending cuts have aroused opposition in parliament on the grounds they will hurt lower-income groups.
Finance Minister Dan Merior has said he is prepared to make spending trade-offs but has refused to increase the total budget.
Croll also warned that proposals to cut aid to service employers would hurt non-merchandise exports and raise costs to the economy.
